Title: Stephan Gerlachs deß Aeltern Tage-Buch der von zween glorwuerdigsten Roemischen Kaeysern Maximiliano und Rudolpho an die Ottomannische Pforte zu Constantinopel abgefertigten und durch David Ungnad, Freyherrn zu Sonnegk und Preyburg, verrichteten Gesandtschafft (the diary of the Tuebingen chaplain Stephan Gerlach at Constantinople, 1573-1578)
Creator: Stephan Gerlach the elder (1546-1612), chaplain to the imperial embassy at Constantinople; published from his papers by his grandson Samuel Gerlach, with a preface by Tobias Wagner
Publisher: Printed by Heinrich Friesen, Frankfurt am Main
Publication Date: 1674
Rights: Public Domain (printed 1674)
Language: deu
Source: Internet Archive item 10330416bsb, file 10330416bsb_djvu.txt (Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Munich, shelfmark 2 It.sing. 23; MDZ scan), fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, one-world agent for Orthodoxy under the Ottomans), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: none given in the item record; the rights basis is the 1674 print date (MDZ's own reuse statement was not consulted, as for the 1584 Acta et scripta already vendored)
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from long s normalised to s (57983 occurrences); the Fraktur hyphenation sign (U+2E17) and the printed marginal notes are left as the OCR gave them. Rights basis restated: a book printed in 1674 is public domain by date.
Content note: SECOND WITNESS (Mark's OCR ruling, 2026-09-25): the Fraktur OCR is readable word by word, but the page's two columns and its marginal glosses are interleaved line by line, so sentences run into each other and no passage can be quoted without checking the page images. Order in the file: MDZ catalogue stub, title page (about line 100-130, imprint 'Getruckt bey Heinrich Friesen, 1674'), Wagner's preface ('Ausfuehrliche Vorrede', from about line 234, including a 'Vorrede vom Tuerck. Reich'), then the diary itself, kept by date from 1573 to 1578 with month and day headings as printed (for example 'Anno 1577.' at about line 50198), and a Register (index) from about line 59617. Gerlach records his visits to Patriarch Jeremias II and Theodosios Zygomalas and the carrying of the Tuebingen letters; an outside Lutheran eyewitness, not the church's own voice. German.
